final_codebook.domain: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers (including regrouping and simplification)

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Determine a least/common denominator (LCD/LCM) and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions with that shared denominator before subtracting.
inclusion_criteria: The work explicitly finds an LCD/LCM of denominators
The work rewrites at least one fraction to an equivalent fraction with a new denominator so the denominators match (e.g., 5/6 -> 15/18)
exclusion_criteria: Fractions already share a denominator and no denominator change is performed
Only mixed-to-improper conversion is done while keeping the same denominator (no LCD step is shown)

skills.name: Subtract fractions
skills.definition: Compute the difference of two fractions once they are expressed with the same denominator by subtracting numerators and keeping the denominator.
inclusion_criteria: Subtracts fractions with like denominators (e.g., (a-b)/d), including after an LCD conversion
Subtracts the fractional parts within a mixed-number subtraction when denominators match
exclusion_criteria: Only whole-number subtraction is performed with no fractional subtraction
Only simplification/reduction or final formatting is performed without a subtraction operation

skills.name: Rewrite mixed/whole forms
skills.definition: Rewrite numbers into equivalent mixed, improper, or whole-plus-fraction forms to enable subtraction and/or to combine whole and fractional parts.
inclusion_criteria: Converts a mixed number to an improper fraction (or vice versa) as part of the solution method
Rewrites a whole number as a mixed number with a fractional part (e.g., 2 = 1 3/3 or 0/d) to set up subtraction
Combines a computed whole part and fractional part into a single mixed-number form (without being primarily a simplification/reduction step)
exclusion_criteria: The key operation is borrowing/regrouping after a negative fractional difference appears (tag S04)
The key operation is reducing a fraction to lowest terms or simplifying 0/d to 0 (tag S04)

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: Regroup by borrowing 1 from the whole part to fix a negative fractional subtraction and/or simplify the resulting value by reducing fractions and expressing 0/d as 0.
inclusion_criteria: Borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it to d/d (or adds d/d to the fractional part) to make the fractional part nonnegative
Reduces a fraction to lowest terms (e.g., 9/12 -> 3/4)
Simplifies 0/d to 0 as part of final cleanup
exclusion_criteria: Only finds an LCD and rewrites equivalent fractions (tag S01)
Only performs the numerator subtraction with like denominators (tag S02)
Only converts between mixed and improper forms without borrowing or reduction (tag S03)

decisions.details: Kept C01 as S01 (Common denominator conversion).
decisions.reasoning: C01 had 3/3 consensus and is a distinct, consistently identifiable operation that precedes many fraction subtractions.
C02 had 3/3 consensus and captures the core computation step once like denominators are established.

decisions.details: Refined C03 into S03 (Rewrite mixed/whole forms) with clearer boundaries versus borrowing (S04) and simplification (S04).
decisions.reasoning: C03 had 2/3 consensus but is diagnostically useful across items that require converting mixed/whole representations; refinement prevents overlap with regrouping and reduction.

decisions.details: Merged C04 + C05 into S04 (Regroup and simplify).
decisions.reasoning: C04 had only 1/3 consensus as a standalone skill, and A/C already bundle borrowing with simplification; combining preserves the common instructional pattern while keeping the final codebook to exactly four distinct skills.

summary: The unified codebook retains the three 3/3-consensus skills (common-denominator conversion, fraction subtraction, and simplification/finalization) and adds a refined mixed/whole rewriting skill (2/3 consensus). Borrowing/regrouping (1/3 as standalone) is merged with simplification to match the dominant expert structure and maintain four clear, non-overlapping skills.
